criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the main behavior claims against the code paths at lines 16-90. The biggest issue is that the 'authoritative' local append at line 82 is not verified before the derived PostHog emission path at lines 85-90, so a projection can exist without the supposed source-of-truth record. I also checked transcript-derived fields and found `started_at` at line 43 depends on file order rather than earliest timestamp. Those are real behavior defects, so this falls below the pass line.

The artifact includes the expected parts: disable override (20-26), transcript metrics (35-55), optional meta fields (56-63), record construction (65-78), authoritative append (80-82), and optional PostHog projection (84-90). The gap is failure-mode coverage: obvious local write failures around 81-82 are not handled before continuing, so completeness is solid but not thorough.

I checked visible house conventions: hook placement and naming are fine, there are no hardcoded secrets, and the artifact keeps a lean local-record-plus-adapter shape. But the rubric explicitly calls out source-of-truth discipline, and lines 82-90 allow the derived PostHog state to diverge from the declared local source of truth because projection is not conditioned on append success.

I actively checked for the main anti-patterns in this rubric: over-engineered collector/platform resurrection, tombstoned measurement-store choices, hardcoded secrets, fabricated content capture, and unnecessary duplicated state. The implementation stays lean: one local JSONL record plus an optional derived adapter, with content-gated counts only and no live tombstone hits. I found no anti-pattern defect of consequence.

I inspected failure visibility on `cd`, `jq`, record build, append, and `curl`. The implementation is quiet not only on success but also on many failures: parse/build errors are redirected to `/dev/null` and exit 0 (lines 17, 38-43, 76), and network failures are swallowed with `|| true` at line 90. That makes telemetry loss difficult to explain or debug, so diagnostics is below the pass line.

defects.description: The script does not check whether the append-only source-of-truth write succeeded before moving on to the derived projection path. If the local append fails (permissions, disk full, directory race), PostHog can still receive an event, so behavior no longer matches the file's own authoritative-record-first contract.

This weakens source-of-truth discipline: the derived adapter is gated only on key presence, not on a successful authoritative local write. Backend telemetry can therefore diverge from the declared `.claude/artifacts/build-sessions.jsonl` source of truth.

Record-construction failures are suppressed to `/dev/null` and exit silently; later network failures are also swallowed. That leaves missing telemetry hard to diagnose and contradicts the comment-level expectation that stop hooks surface a `systemMessage` when there is something to report.
`started_at` is taken from the first transcript entry as stored, not the earliest timestamp. If transcript order is not strictly chronological, the emitted session start time will be inaccurate.

All main parts are present, but obvious filesystem failure handling around `mkdir -p`/append is missing before the script continues. Failure-mode coverage is therefore thinner than a production telemetry hook normally needs.
